answer: The statistically most enriched GO biological process CANNOT be determined from the supplied capsule, because the capsule contains no GO-BP gene-set annotation (gencode 'ont' column is 100% empty; the HGNC file's 11 columns carry no GO field; whole-filesystem searches for obo/gaf/gmt/gene2go were empty; the environment is offline with no R/Bioconductor or GO packages), so a statistically valid gene-to-GO enrichment test cannot be executed on these inputs. Executed deliverable is the approved DE pipeline in pure Python: subset to the 14 coldata samples (dropping MGD1640F/MGD1641F), PAR_Y duplicate collapse (60,662 -> 60,617 genes), rowSums>=10 filter (31,149 genes tested; 16,203 protein_coding), median-of-ratios size factors, NB GLM ~ condition with trend-based dispersion shrinkage + Wald + BH. Results: 1,541 DE genes at BH padj<0.05 (832 up / 709 down in disease); 970 at |log2FC|>1 & padj<0.05; sex-adjusted sensitivity gives 1,207 significant with 1,082 overlap and r=0.93 (log10 padj), i.e. highly concordant. Best interim (informal, NOT a statistical enrichment): the top DE genes span ECM/connective-tissue (COMP, VCAN, ADAMTS1/5, IGFBP2/3, PDGFRB, CCN5), developmental/HOX (HOTAIR, HOXC11/12, ALX4, LUZP2), neuronal (STMN2, CNTN4, GNAO1, PCDH19, KCND2, CLSTN2) and immune-modulatory (TNFSF18, STEAP4, PI16) sets, heuristically suggesting GO-BP themes such as extracellular-matrix organization, skeletal system development, regulation of cell differentiation, and nervous system development - pending any GO annotation source to rank them statistically.
